activities.anchor: That is not a limitation philosophy chose; it is what physics offers cheaply
activities.caption: file each design by how it weathers noise
activities.name: binNoiseSort

config.prompt: Two engineering bets walk into a noisy world — file each design:

items.label: a switch asked only 'high or low?' despite drifting voltage
ten distinct voltage levels stored per cell
a bit that stays readable as temperature and interference drift
decimal-style cells that misread a neighbouring value when the circuit warms
the lesson's founding bet: reliability beats compactness
a narrow ladder of voltages where each rung is a rounding mistake away from its neighbour

config.why: Two states survive noise and ten do not — a wide margin beats a dense code, and everything in the lesson follows from that one trade.

activities.anchor: the master pattern of the whole subject is arithmetic, not magic
activities.caption: pair each bit width with what it names
activities.name: binBitsMatch

config.prompt: Pair each width with the box of values it opens:

pairs.right: 256 values, ceiling 255 — room for one typed letter
65,536 values — the 16-bit era of games and sound
about 4 billion locations — the wall 2000s PCs actually hit
eight symbols — enough that 2³ covers a small alphabet

config.why: n bits give 2ⁿ distinct values, and one extra bit doubles the count — which is why memory sizes come in powers of two.

activities.anchor: A merchant's balance makes the uniqueness visible
activities.caption: complete the place-value sentence
activities.name: binPlaceCloze

config.text: Binary is a place-value system like decimal, only the base differs: 1101 means 1×%%0%% + 1×4 + 0×%%1%% + 1×1 = %%2%%. To go from denary, repeatedly subtract the %%3%% power of two that fits; to go back, %%4%% the place values under every 1.
config.hint: One weight of each size — 1, 2, 4, 8 — and each power either fits or it does not, so the spelling comes out exact.

activities.caption: find the faulty line — two's complement, worked
activities.name: binTwosSpot

config.prompt: One step of this negative-number working is wrong — click it:
lines: To store −13 in 8 bits, start from its positive spelling, 00001101.
The same adder does both jobs: a − b runs as a + (−b) — nothing extra to build.
The 8-bit range runs from −256 to +255, so stepping past the top simply keeps counting.
config.correction: Eight bits hold −128 to +127: the ceiling is 127, and 127 + 1 wraps around to −128 — the arithmetic version of an odometer rolling over.
config.why: Flip-and-add-1 makes each negation sum to zero by ordinary addition — but the range stays fixed, and stepping past it is the overflow error.

activities.caption: bet before you read on — the mojibake mystery
activities.name: binTextPredict

config.q: You open a document and find 'cafÃ©' where 'café' should be. What happened?
choices: The bytes are unchanged — the program decoded them with a different character dictionary
Some bytes were lost in transmission, truncating the accented letter
The accent was never stored: plain English text costs one byte per letter
The author typed it wrong — editors never misinterpret stored bytes
config.why: The bytes are identical; a dictionary between integers and symbols was applied that disagrees with the one used at write time. Once text is integers, any mismatched lookup shows exactly this.

activities.anchor: you must sample at better than twice the highest frequency
activities.caption: call the size of one stereo minute
activities.name: binSoundEst

config.prompt: One minute of stereo music, CD quality — 44,100 measurements each second, 16 bits per measurement, two channels — how much storage, before compression?
config.why: 44,100 × 16 × 2 × 60 ≈ 10.1 million bytes ≈ 10.6 MB — rate × resolution × channels × seconds, straight from the dials.
config.context: Roughly three MP3s of the same minute — which is why lossy compression is structural, not optional.

activities.anchor: Nothing is missing; two definitions of
activities.caption: where does the 'missing' 7% go?
activities.name: binDrivePlace

config.prompt: A drive sold as '1 TB' — one decimal trillion bytes — where does its shown size land on this binary scale?
config.why: Divide 1,000,000,000,000 by 1,024, three times over: 931.32. Every byte is present — the label counts powers of ten while the operating system measures powers of 2.

activities.anchor: The ratios are dramatic (10:1 is normal)
activities.caption: one archive job, three assets, one rule
activities.name: binCompBranch

config.root: One backup drive, several assets, and one question each time: must the meaning survive exactly, or is the appearance the point?

choices.label: Lossless (ZIP)
choices.feedback: Bit-for-bit survives — a single altered character is a bug, so this was never a lossy candidate.

choices.label: Lossy, tuned for pictures
choices.feedback: A changed letter in a program is not smaller art; it is a bug. Code has almost no repetition to trade, either.

srcOk.text: Code archived intact. Next: a photo of a smooth grey sky.

choices.label: JPEG (lossy)
choices.feedback: Roughly 10× smaller, and what gets thrown away sits where the eye is least sensitive.

choices.label: Run-length or dictionary (lossless)
choices.feedback: Safe but barely smaller — smooth tones have almost no repeated runs or phrases to describe.

srcBad.text: A 'compressed' program that behaves differently is broken, not compressed — restart the job with lossless.

photoOk.text: Pictures done. Last: the concert recording.

choices.label: MP3 (lossy)
choices.feedback: Masked frequencies go, perceived sound stays — psychoacoustics decides what may be dropped.

choices.label: A bit-for-bit audio archive
choices.feedback: Every sample survives, at many times the size — the right call only when the recording itself must be preserved exactly.

photoOk2.text: Big but exact. Last: the concert recording.

choices.label: MP3 (lossy)
choices.feedback: Masked frequencies go, perceived sound stays — psychoacoustics decides what may be dropped.

choices.label: A bit-for-bit audio archive
choices.feedback: Every sample survives, at many times the size — the right call only when the recording itself must be preserved exactly.

musicOk.text: Archive complete: code exact, pictures and audio at a fraction of the size, nothing you would notice gone.

musicOk2.text: Archive complete: everything exact, at the cost of a much fuller drive.

config.why: The rule: if meaning must survive exactly — text, records, programs — lossless only; if appearance is the point — pictures, sound — throwing away barely-perceived detail is the honest bargain.
